fallback.text: Aeneid 1.1, Arma virumque canō, Troiae quī prīmus ab ōrīs, scans – ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ ⏑ | – – | – – | – ⏑ ⏑ | – –: dactyl, dactyl, spondee, spondee, dactyl, and a final spondee (DDSSDS), 15 syllables, with the main caesura after canō, after the third long syllable (penthemimeral). The seven opening lines: 1 DDSSDS, 2 DSDSDS, 3 DSSSDS (with the elisions mult(um) ill(e) et), 4 DSDSDS, 5 DSSSDS, 6 SDDDDS, 7 SDSSDS.
